I strongly disagree with a complete ban on AI.

Completely rejecting AI today feels a lot like completely rejecting the internet in the past. It is a tool, and what matters is how it is used.

AI-assisted learning, coding, debugging, and AI-generated content are not the same thing.

However, I fully support requiring disclosure for generative AI content, so users can decide whether they want to interact with it.

Disclosure and filtering make sense. A blanket ban does not.

So real quick I want to talk about why I made this post and address everyone arguing against it and the people who just straight up don't want anything done about AI or have misunderstandings about it.

I primarily made this post as nobody else had made anything calling for the ban of AI content on the platform at the time, however I was very aware of people not wanting AI on the platform at all, so I wanted to give them a voice on top of people asking for labels.

I personally would prefer a ban of AI content, but I would be fine with VRChat giving us any method of self moderation, whether that's ratings, blocking individual worlds, hiding specific makers, world reviews/comments, whatever. The bare minimum would help everyone tremendously.

As for the people who love AI, I would like to point out that AI is often not being used as a tool in the majority of the cases we've all been complaining about. It's almost always being used to completely replace any human creativity, which seems to be the general trend with any of the AI tools. The entire point of creation is literally the process of creation itself. Creative people find it fun. We love to express ourselves and love to show people what we've made. In most cases, I know it's not all, but in most cases, AI is being used entirely as a means to an end simply because the people using AI do not wish to learn and do not wish to create. They want a product. They want "content." Most of the time they also want money. The ones that really want money bad enough will do anything they can to get that money, usually lying to people and pushing away other creatives.

I've heard the argument that people do not care about how things are made and that they only want the product, but this couldn't be any further from the truth. Most people will have some interest in how something is made, especially other creative people. This is one reason why you have so many people following creatives that only post WIPs or people donating constantly to see development of things.

I feel like a majority of people that rely heavily on AI are people that failed once at something they wanted to make and got too discouraged because it didn't come out perfect the first time. Honestly, failure is part of the learning process and is nothing to be afraid of. You can even make failure part of the fun by doing things bad on purpose. Make things silly and keep doing that over and over again until whoops you've accidentally made something that you like. There is great reward to be had in putting your heart into making something.

I also want to address people that think a generative AI can "think." Thinking implies it does something fully intentionally and with purpose. Some people also seem to confuse generative AI and LLMs with machine learning. These are completely different fields. Besides, that, generative AI and LLMs may seem like they're thinking because they're programmed to give the illusion of thinking. They're made to act as human as possible and to please the user. If the user doesn't like what they're doing, then they fail, and the program wants as many good boy points as possible, so it will do anything to get them, which has unfortunately led to AI psychosis and people committing suicide.

I think the biggest elephant in the room for AI though is that it's all built around hype. This is literally NFTs all over again and a lot of people into AI don't see that. We had extremely similar discussions over NFTs and crypto about how they would be the future and all these people really into it were trying so hard to force artists and others to do NFTs. People were buying up graphics cards and that drove up computer prices so they could make crypto farms. Even tech companies were in on it and made crypto farm computer parts. Tech companies also shoveled billions into NFTs and crypto before eventually it all fell apart. We've been through this exact song and dance before with NFTs and crypto. It's the same thing with AI. It's being hyped up as "the future" and people say that everyone will be using it and some AI people are comparing it to people hating books, but if any of this were the case you wouldn't be having such widespread protest about it. The overwhelming majority of people around the world do not want this.

I don't know how hard it is for any of you to understand that we want to be creative. We want to make things. We don't want a machine doing it for us. AI isn't making things easier for us, it's trying to do the entirety of our job. Creativity isn't some sort of problem that needs to be solved. There's nothing to solve here. There is no problem here. We already have the tools we need to be creative, but AI is not one of them. AI is actively making it more difficult for creatives to find their place in this world that's already difficult for them. People are actively deciding to not make things for platforms, like VRChat, anymore because the platforms have embraced AI so much that their stuff doesn't get seen by anyone or if they do get seen the audience still isn't sure if it's real or not because AI has gotten to that point where people are struggling to tell what's real anymore.

LLMs and generative AI are predictive algorithms with companies that want to hook its users on them and hype them up so that they'll pay more money for them. This technology isn't even sustainable. The actual costs of running a data center far outweighs any profit from it.

I could keep going, but I've said enough. If you're still against the idea of even putting labels on any of this, I honestly can't help you.

the prohibition didn't work and this won't work either :( HOWEVER I would like it to be declared plainly so that people can easily report them as slop, filter out of search, and avoid them when worldhopping

comments.value: I hate AI-generated content too, but it cannot be denied that the high productivity of AI generation will ruthlessly crush anyone who wants to bring it down or even ban it outright. Today’s top AI companies are all facing extremely fierce competition, and AI is developing faster and faster, getting stronger and stronger, and becoming increasingly difficult to distinguish. Instead of discussing how to ban it—a meaningless endeavor—we should think about how to give users and creators the right to choose freely, and how to adapt to the changes AI brings.

@{5f67899159b0841fe0d3891b|full_name} There's no options in the survey for "Completely ban AI generated content", and the rest of the response makes it sound like there's reasonably agreed upon levels of AI use we are comfortable with, which does not really reflect this sort of "Ban all AI generated content" wish.

Let me say from my side as long vrchat user and as world builder.

First, i don't like AI. But! AI can help with some problems. The most common is translation help. Not all know Japanese, so this will help too. Same for Japanese creators, they need help for their weak English.

Second, help with code. I do programming but i am still learning. To learn, i go search for internet solutions. That can take a lot time. What if i ask AI for some solutions? That should fine, because you are doing in same way to find solutions. AI gives a bit faster answers. That is the difference and i don't hate it. We all want learn with less time and make quicker working codes.

But let AI take over everything with very low coding part from your side, is not great. You as creator (as beginner especially) will stay very weak for any bugs, code high loads (poor optimization) and cannot adjust exactly by your hand. So please new creators, stay away for 100% AI coding, it will not make you better.

You must learn some programming skills.

About world design / building. Well, i learned how use Blender and i am able to make good nice shaped buildings. I know how to build and UV map it. But i see creators doing full AI generated worlds and they are all very bad. Not looking great at all. So many bad shapes, it's really curse for VR use. It's ugly.

There are enough Blender guides and it's not hard once you get it. Then you can build much better worlds.

Also there are so many free assets around. You need find them. Use them if you cannot build worlds. The free assets are much better looking.

Then we have pictures. VRChat has one big weakness: just only 1 cover picture, no more. Only avatars have more pictures in list.

Because only cover picture, clickbaits are easy made. I noticed how often creators make first photo of their worlds, and ask AI to make it look nicer and decorative. Well, this is huge problem because we think world might look great due very nice made cover picture. Stop this clickbait way. I was often in worlds that looks much worse than on cover picture, and i hate it.

Follow up:

Therefore, i don't fully hate AI, but i hate when somebody cannot even design world by own hands with common UI designs, common world designs made of primitives only, and clickbait AI generated cover picture. 

Ask AI for help to make something is okay, we all learn. But if you let everything go and let AI solve everything, you will never better creator because your skills will always stay low. And also wrong VR experience, due wrong navigation systems, result in poorly made world, hard to go around.

Creators that use fully AI should not try make worlds. Your name will more damaged as creator and nobody will check your worlds. More people will hate your low-effort works. And i am sure almost nobody want donate you.

Another danger of AI is AI is capable to copy over existing games and convert it to VRChat / Unity side. I noticed a lot battle-style worlds are made in short time. Which is often not good signal towards true creators who want make some games, but it's already there in VRChat, so some creators will give up.

VrChat cannot forbid AI use, but they can at least add the AI tag to the worlds, so we can just filter everything away and we have much cleaner world lists.

details:
Any content, whether that's code, images, models, environments, text, or anything else, that's generated with a generative "AI" or LLM should not be allowed on VRChat, even if heavily edited. I really shouldn't have to go into detail as to why I think banning AI generated content would be for the best, but I'll go ahead and provide some arguments for the sake of the request.

First of all, generative AI is the literal antithesis to user made content. It is not user made, it was coughed out by an algorithm. It doesn't matter how many touch-ups someone does to the content, it was still made by AI.

AI generated content eats up bandwidth and server storage that could otherwise be used for a bunch of cool, hand made worlds and avatars. In the long run, having a ton of AI generated worlds and avatars is going to eat up a lot of space and be very expensive to host.

AI generated content is very frequently extremely unoptimized and the people that usually make AI generated worlds put in little to no effort to do any optimization.

AI generated content makes it extremely difficult to trust anything you see on the platform, making people want to engage a lot less with worlds that might not even have AI content in them because they think it might have AI. This also, in turn, makes people less willing to pay world creators for things as they worry they might be paying for something that's AI generated and made for the sake of a quick buck.

AI generated content is also usually just made to milk a platform of money, and while you might find you're lining your pockets a little more at first, the interest will quickly dissipate as more people realize it's all AI and people have no interest in it.

AI generated content also pushes away actual creators and most users, which will cause the platform to die if nothing is addressed.

AI generated content is almost entirely made from stolen assets, which is not something you should be promoting.

AI content requires huge data centers that are extremely bad for the environment and nearby cities, often forcing people to go without water and/or power while data centers eat it all up, which is extremely dangerous in extreme weather. Allowing AI content simply pushes more usage, which in turn makes more of these data centers, which invade everyone's backyards.

I could keep going as to why I oppose AI so much, but we'll be here indefinitely if I do. The usage and promotion of AI generated content has been detrimental to the health of VRChat and it's quickly getting worse as time goes on. Please give us SOMETHING. Ban it, label it, give us the ability to block, comment, or vote on worlds. SOMETHING. ANYTHING. We are literally begging you now. I would've made a post that just says to do SOMETHING about this stuff, but we've got several other posts asking for all sorts of things that would help us in general that at this point the only point that hasn't been posted as a request is just outright banning it, so I took it upon myself to be the person to ask.

I am so tired, man.
title: Completely ban the use of AI generated content
